gold_answer: In 2003, the claim was supported as the dominant model, assuming a single transition state. By 2010, Schmid et al.'s NMR data revealed multiple enamine geometries, showing the Houk-List transition state is only one limit under specific conditions, leading to revision: the mechanism is enamine-based but stereo-determination is substrate-dependent, making the original claim too absolute.
source_titles: ch05_p1: Proline-Catalyzed Direct Asymmetric Aldol Reactions; ch05_p2: Transition States of Amine-Catalyzed Aldol Reactions Involving Enamine Intermediates: Theoretical Studies of Mechanism, Reactivity, and Stereoselectivity; ch05_p3: Quantum Mechanical Predictions of the Stereoselectivities of Proline-Catalyzed Asymmetric Intermolecular Aldol Reactions; ch05_p4: The Elusive Enamine Intermediate in ProlineCatalyzed Aldol Reactions: NMR Detection, Formation Pathway, and Stabilization Trends
evidence_text:
source_arc:ch05:ch05:evidence_evolution [revises] List/Lerner/Barbas 2000 demonstrated proline-catalyzed direct asymmetric aldol. Bahmanyar & Houk 2001/2003 computed enamine transition state predicting stereochemistry - Houk-List model. Schmid/Zeitler/Gschwind 2010 NMR studies of proline enamine intermediates revealed populations and exchange consistent with multiple TS geometries; the simple Houk-List picture is one limit. Mechanism is enamine-based but stereo-determining TS depends on substrate.
source_arc:ch05:ch05:expert_note [scopes] Mechanism-refined arc. Good for QA on 'what the original model got right and what it had to be revised on.' DOI/citation verified: Schmid et al. is Angew Chem Int Ed 49:4997-5003, not JACS 132:3010. Expert note: Schmid/Zeitler/Gschwind 2010 directly observes enamine intermediate populations by NMR; it is slightly off-target from transition-state-only claims but defensible for mechanism refinement.

source_arc:ch07:ch07:evidence_evolution [establishes_uncertainty] Walling 1975 codified the HO- mechanism. Pestovsky 2005 spectroscopically identified aqueous Fe(IV)=O. Bataineh 2012 showed pH-dependent mechanistic crossover: HO- at low pH, Fe(IV)=O at neutral pH. The 'just hydroxyl radicals' claim is incomplete; the active oxidant identity depends on pH and ligand environment.
source_arc:ch07:ch07:expert_note [scopes] Mechanism-revised arc with pH-dependent crossover. Excellent for condition-bounded mechanism QA.

gold_answer: The contradiction arises because ligand-free Heck reactions with ultra-low Pd loading (Reetz & de Vries 2004) show homogeneous behavior, implying leached Pd is active, which contradicts the idea of surface catalysis on nanoparticles. This was resolved by de Vries 2006's unified mechanism where nanoparticles act as Pd reservoirs, and Phan et al. 2006's review confirming most 'heterogeneous' systems release molecular species, making surface catalysis rare and context-dependent.
source_titles: ch04_p1: Ligand-free Heck reactions using low Pd-loading; ch04_p2: A unifying mechanism for all high-temperature Heck reactions. The role of palladium colloids and anionic species; ch04_p3: On the Nature of the Active Species in Palladium Catalyzed Mizoroki-Heck and Suzuki-Miyaura Couplings - Homogeneous or Heterogeneous Catalysis, A Critical Review
evidence_text: source_arc:ch04:ch04:evidence_evolution [contradicts] Reetz & de Vries 2004 showed ligand-free, very low-Pd Heck reactions proceed via leached Pd species, suggesting molecular catalyst dominates. de Vries 2006 unified mechanism: nanoparticles act as reservoirs releasing active soluble Pd. Phan, Van Der Sluys & Jones 2006 reviewed 'is it heterogeneous?' literature: most reported 'heterogeneous' Pd catalysts are reservoirs for molecular species; true surface catalysis is rare and depends on substrate/temperature.

gold_answer: To observe stochastic ee, enantiopure starting material must be used with absolutely no optically active additives or chiral impurities. Deviations introduce external chiral bias, which masks the intrinsic stochastic symmetry breaking, thereby invalidating claims of a deterministic mechanism since the outcome becomes externally driven rather than system-generated.
source_titles: ch02_p1: Asymmetric autocatalysis and amplification of enantiomeric excess of a chiral molecule; ch02_p2: Enantioselective Synthesis without Discrete Optically Active Additives; ch02_p3: Asymmetric autocatalysis and its implications for the origin of homochirality
evidence_text:
source_arc:ch02:ch02:evidence_evolution [revises] Soai 1995 reported autocatalytic amplification of ee in alkylation of pyrimidine carbaldehyde. Singleton & Vo 2002 found the reaction can produce high ee from no added chiral influence - apparent stochastic chiral symmetry breaking. Blackmond 2004 proposed a dimer-based kinetic model. Mechanism still partly open; reproducibility constrained by trace chiral contamination control.
source_arc:ch02:ch02:expert_note [scopes] Mechanism-uncertainty arc. Good for 'what is known vs assumed' and reproducibility-condition QA. Expert note: surface the stronger Singleton & Vo point: with enantiopure starting material and no added chirality, macroscopic ee can be stochastically determined.
source_arc:ch02:s2_t2:expert_text [supports] The enantiopure starting material must be used, and crucially, no optically active additives or chiral impurities can be present - even trace contamination can dominate the outcome.

gold_answer: After Varambally 2002, EZH2 was understood as an oncogene driven by overexpression in prostate cancer; after Ernst 2010, the claim was revised to reflect that EZH2 can act as a tumor suppressor via loss-of-function in myeloid contexts, establishing its lineage-context-dependent dual role in cancer.
source_titles: cb08_p1: The polycomb group protein EZH2 is involved in progression of prostate cancer; cb08_p2: Somatic mutations altering EZH2 (Tyr641) in follicular and diffuse large B-cell lymphomas of germinal-center origin; cb08_p3: Inactivating mutations of the histone methyltransferase gene EZH2 in myeloid disorders; cb08_p4: EZH2 Is Required for Germinal Center Formation and Somatic EZH2 Mutations Promote Lymphoid Transformation
evidence_text: source_arc:cb08:cb08:evidence_evolution [revises] Varambally 2002 established EZH2 overexpression as oncogenic driver in prostate cancer. Morin 2010 / Beguelin 2013 found activating Y641 mutations driving GCB-DLBCL and follicular lymphoma. Ernst 2010 reported inactivating EZH2 mutations in MDS/MPN - loss-of-function pathogenic in myeloid disease. EZH2 is therefore lineage-context-dependent: same gene, opposite roles.

gold_answer: No — while p21/CDKN1A is a common companion marker to p16, the Gorgoulis 2019 consensus uses 'p16/p21' to indicate either or both, and heterogeneity means some senescent cells may express only one. The field does not mandate both in all contexts.
source_titles: cb09_p1: Forging a signature of in vivo senescence; cb09_p2: Unmasking Transcriptional Heterogeneity in Senescent Cells; cb09_p3: Cellular Senescence: Defining a Path Forward
evidence_text:
source_arc:cb09:cb09:expert_note [establishes_uncertainty] Definition-evolved arc - the field operationally redefined senescence to a multi-marker requirement. Good 'what counts as evidence' QA. Expert note: treat Gorgoulis 2019 as a field-defining consensus statement; p21/CDKN1A is a common companion marker to p16.
source_arc:cb09:cb09:evidence_evolution [revises] Sharpless & Sherr 2015 reviewed marker landscape and noted p16 expression in non-senescent contexts (immune cells, stem cells). Hernandez-Segura 2017 found senescence signatures heterogeneous across triggers/cell types - no canonical transcriptional core. Gorgoulis 2019 international consensus: senescence requires multi-marker evidence (SA--gal + p16/p21 + SASP + proliferation arrest), no single marker is sufficient.

gold_answer: The contradiction was resolved by distinguishing ordered domains from intrinsically disordered regions: Ruff & Pappu 2021 showed that low pLDDT in IDRs reflects biological disorder, not algorithmic failure, meaning AlphaFold2 is accurately signaling uncertainty rather than making incorrect predictions.
source_titles: cb04_p1: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold; cb04_p2: A structural biology community assessment of AlphaFold2 applications; cb04_p3: AlphaFold and Implications for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins; cb04_p4: Impact of protein conformational diversity on AlphaFold predictions
evidence_text:
source_arc:cb04:cb04:expert_note [contradicts] Headline claim is right but scope-bounded. Useful for teaching scope/condition reasoning rather than contradiction. Expert note: do not describe Akdel as only IDR-focused; distinguish IDRs from conformational diversity.
source_arc:cb04:cb04:evidence_evolution [revises] Jumper 2021 reports CASP14-level accuracy for many ordered protein domains. Akdel 2022 is a broad community assessment across applications including drug discovery, complexes, and IDPs. Ruff & Pappu 2021 is the clean IDR-specific source: low pLDDT often marks disorder rather than ordinary structural error. Saldano 2022 shows conformational-diversity limits: AlphaFold often converges to one conformer even where multiple experimentally known states exist.

gold_answer: Collectively, these studies show that tumor-cell PD-L1 scoring is relatively consistent across assays (except SP142 undercalling), immune-cell scoring has high inter-assay and inter-reader variability, and clinical decisions must account for both assay identity and cell-type scope. Rimm 2017 confirms that pathologist disagreement is higher for immune-cell counts, reinforcing that context—not just assay—is critical.
source_titles: cb05_p1: PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry Assays for Lung Cancer: Results from Phase 1 of the Blueprint PD-L1 IHC Assay Comparison Project; cb05_p2: PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry Comparability Study in Real-Life Clinical Samples: Results of Blueprint Phase 2 Project; cb05_p3: A Prospective, Multi-institutional, Pathologist-Based Assessment of 4 Immunohistochemistry Assays for PD-L1 Expression in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
evidence_text: source_arc:cb05:cb05:evidence_evolution [scopes] Blueprint Phase 1 (Hirsch 2017) found three of four assays broadly concordant for tumor-cell PD-L1 scoring, with SP142 lower. Blueprint Phase 2 (Tsao 2018) showed immune-cell scoring varies more strongly across assays and pathologists. Rimm 2017 reported inter-assay and inter-reader variation. The arc is tumor-cell versus immune-cell scope, not a direct flip-flop.

gold_answer: The claim evolved from Zhang 2009's theoretical prediction of surface-state-dominated transport to Analytis 2010's experimental finding that as-grown Bi2Se3 exhibits bulk-dominated transport due to Se vacancy n-doping, with surface transport only observable after bulk carrier suppression.
source_titles: ms06_p1: Topological insulators in Bi2Se3, Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3 with a single Dirac cone on the surface; ms06_p2: Observation of a large-gap topological-insulator class with a single Dirac cone on the surface; ms06_p3: A tunable topological insulator in the spin helical Dirac transport regime; ms06_p4: Two-dimensional surface state in the quantum limit of a topological insulator
evidence_text: source_arc:ms06:ms06:evidence_evolution [revises] Zhang 2009 (theory) predicted Bi2Se3 as 3D TI with single Dirac cone. Xia 2009 and Hsieh 2009 demonstrated topological surface state by ARPES/spin-resolved ARPES. Analytis 2010 transport measurements: as-grown crystals are heavily n-doped by Se vacancies - bulk conduction dominates, surface fraction recovered only with Ca compensation or thin-film tuning. Surface-state physics is real but transport identification requires explicit suppression of bulk carriers.

source_arc:ms04:ms04:evidence_evolution [establishes_uncertainty] Murugan 2007 reported cubic LLZO with ~ 10^-4 S/cm at RT. Awaka 2009 showed undoped LLZO crystallizes as the lower-conductivity tetragonal phase at RT - the original 'pure cubic' samples were inadvertently Al-stabilized from Al2O3 crucibles. Geiger 2011 systematically established Al substitution requirements for cubic stabilization. Buschmann 2011 reviewed structural and dynamic measurements. The high-conductivity cubic phase is only achievable with aliovalent doping; 'undoped LLZO' is poorly conductive.
source_arc:ms04:ms04:expert_note [scopes] Synthesis-artifact arc - original 'pure cubic' was a doped sample. Excellent for QA on hidden experimental confounds. Expert note: highlight inadvertent Al from alumina crucibles; Geiger 2011 shows about 0.5 Al per formula unit in early nominally pure LLZO.

gold_answer: The papers show progressive recognition that Cu isn't a passive substrate. Li 2009 established surface-limited monolayer growth on untreated foil (polycrystalline). Yan 2012 demonstrated mm-scale grains via long pretreatment, hinting at surface control. Hao 2013 identified trace oxygen as the specific suppressor of nucleation density to 4 nuclei/cm², enabling cm-scale single crystals. Together they reveal Cu surface state as the hidden variable controlling graphene quality.
source_titles: ms08_p1: Large-Area Synthesis of High-Quality and Uniform Graphene Films on Copper Foils; ms08_p2: Toward the Synthesis of Wafer-Scale Single-Crystal Graphene on Copper Foils; ms08_p3: The Role of Surface Oxygen in the Growth of Large Single-Crystal Graphene on Copper
evidence_text: source_arc:ms08:ms08:evidence_evolution [revises] Li 2009 demonstrated low-pressure CVD on Cu foil - surface-limited self-terminating monolayer growth. Yan 2012 produced large grains (~mm) using long-pretreatment and growth control. Hao 2013 demonstrated that trace surface oxygen on Cu suppresses nucleation density, enabling cm-scale single crystals. Cu surface state (oxidation, roughness, pretreatment) sets nucleation density and grain size - same gas chemistry, different Cu pretreatment, very different graphene quality.

gold_answer: Critical method constraints include using a carefully selected pressure range (p/p0 < 0.1, per Walton & Snurr 2007) and avoiding thermal activation for fragile MOFs in favor of supercritical CO2 (Nelson 2009). Critical condition constraints include the MOF’s structural fragility (e.g., HKUST-1, NU-110), solvent history (incomplete removal blocks pores), and the need for tailored solvent-exchange protocols (Farha 2012). Reproducibility requires matching all these method and condition parameters across experiments.

evidence_text:
paper:ms07_p2:ms07_p2:conclusion [scopes] They concluded BET can be used for microporous MOFs if the pressure range is chosen carefully to avoid overestimation in micropore filling regions.
paper:ms07_p3:ms07_p3:conclusion [scopes] Supercritical CO2 activation recovers approximately 50% more surface area than thermal activation for fragile MOFs.
paper:ms07_p4:ms07_p4:method [scopes] Ultrahigh surface areas depend strongly on solvent-exchange and activation protocol — gentle removal of guests and prevention of framework collapse are critical.
source_arc:ms07:ms07:evidence_evolution [scopes] Chui 1999 introduced HKUST-1. Walton & Snurr 2007 evaluated BET applicability to microporous frameworks and found its assumptions are stretched but acceptable with proper pressure-range selection. Nelson 2009 showed supercritical CO2 activation recovers ~50% more surface area than thermal activation for fragile MOFs. Farha 2012 produced ultrahigh-surface-area MOFs (NU-110, ~7000 m2/g BET) with strong dependence on solvent-exchange and activation. 'MOF BET area' depends heavily on activation choice and BET fitting protocol.
